title: Conches sound and Arjuna's chariot rolls forward

verses.sa: तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः । सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥
verses.tr: The elder of the Kuru clan, the powerful grandfather Bhishma, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, filling Duryodhana with joy.
verses.angle: Bhishma answers fear with a lion's roar
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Duryodhana orders his men to protect Bhishma, and the old commander answers with a blast of his conch.

body.text: The elder of the Kuru clan, the powerful grandfather Bhishma, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, filling Duryodhana with joy. Bhishma does not speak. He roars like a lion and blows his conch loudly, and the sound fills Duryodhana with joy because the old man has read the king's fear and answered it with a signal to fight. Then the whole battlefield erupts as both armies sound their own battle horns at once.

verses.sa: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः । सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥
verses.tr: Then conches, kettledrums, drums, and trumpets burst forth at once. Their sound became thunderous.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya describes the moment the battlefield fills with sound, as every instrument of war answers Bhishma's call.

body.text: Then conches, kettledrums, drums, and trumpets burst forth at once. Their sound became thunderous. The word sahaseva means all at once, and it reveals the sudden, unified roar of the entire army joining their commander. Then Madhava and the Pandava sound their own divine conches from their great chariot.

verses.sa: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ । माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥
verses.tr: Then, seated on the great chariot yoked with white horses, Madhava and Pandava blew their divine conches.
verses.angle: Two names, one chariot, one sound
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: The Kaurava war cries have just filled the air. Now, from the other side, two conches answer at once. Listen for who is blowing them.

body.text: Then, seated on the great chariot yoked with white horses, Madhava and Pandava blew their divine conches. Madhava and Pandava, two names, but they sit together on one chariot. The verse names them side by side, showing they are moving as one. Krishna blows the Panchajanya and Arjuna the Devadatta, answering the enemy noise with their own divine sound.

verses.sa: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः । पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥
verses.tr: Hrisikesha Krishna blew the Panchajanya, Dhananjaya Arjuna blew the Devadatta, and Bhima of mighty deeds blew the great conch Paundra.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Listen for the names of the conches that sound at the start of the war. Three great warriors are named here.

body.text: Hrisikesha Krishna blew the Panchajanya, Dhananjaya Arjuna blew the Devadatta, and Bhima of mighty deeds blew the great conch Paundra. Each conch has its own name, Panchajanya, Devadatta, and Paundra. These are named possessions of the three greatest warriors on the Pandava side. The conches of the remaining Pandava brothers follow, marking the full array of the army.

verses.sa: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥
verses.tr: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
verses.angle: King Yudhishthira and the twins answer
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: The Pandava conches have already sounded. Now the remaining three brothers join the call. Listen to who blows what.

body.text: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and Manipushpaka. The verse names three brothers in a line, but the order matters. Yudhishthira, the king and eldest, blows first, and the twins Nakula and Sahadeva answer with their own conches right after him. The next verse lists the warriors who follow the Pandava brothers into the fray.

verses.sa: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः । धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥
verses.tr: The great archer from Kashi, Shikhandi the great warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and invincible Satyaki.
verses.angle: Every ally on the Pandava side is heard
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: After the five Pandavas, Sanjaya lists the allies who answer the call to battle. Listen for the next names.

body.text: The great archer from Kashi, Shikhandi the great warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and invincible Satyaki. The names Shikhandi and Dhrishtadyumna belong to the same family, yet they stand on the Pandava side. This shows that the war has already divided the Panchala kingdom itself. Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and Abhimanyu also blew their conches, so the sound of war spreads further.

verses.sa: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते । सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
verses.tr: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and mighty Abhimanyu each blew their conches separately, O lord of the earth.
verses.angle: Each sounding his own conch separately
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya has just finished naming the great warriors on the Pandava side, and now he describes the sound they make. Listen to how each one claims his own space.

body.text: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and mighty Abhimanyu each blew their conches separately, O lord of the earth. Notice the last two words of the verse, separately each. Drupada, the five sons of Draupadi, and Abhimanyu each sound their own conches. That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth.

verses.sa: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् । नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥
verses.tr: That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth.
verses.angle: Vyadarayat, to rip open the hearts
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: The Pandava conches sound, and the noise is so fierce it seems to shake the very ground. Listen for who it strikes.

body.text: That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth. The word vyadarayat means to rip open or split. The sound of the Pandava conches rips open the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons before a single weapon is lifted. Yet Arjuna, the source of this sound, does not stand in joy. He lifts his bow, ready to fight.

verses.sa: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः । प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥
verses.tr: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing in battle order while the weapons were about to begin, Arjuna lifted his bow.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Notice the exact instant the Gita freezes. Listen for the banner and the bow.

body.text: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing in battle order while the weapons were about to begin, Arjuna lifted his bow. Notice the word kapidhvajah, meaning he whose banner bears Hanuman. The banner on Arjuna's chariot carries the monkey god, a sign of devotion, right at the edge of a war that will destroy the very world that worships him. Arjuna asks Krishna to stop the chariot between the two armies so he can look at the faces of the men he is about to fight.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचहृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, place my chariot between the two armies, O Achyuta, until I can look at these men who wish to fight and see with whom I must battle in this war.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has raised his bow, but now he stops. He asks his charioteer to turn the chariot and show him the men on the field.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, place my chariot between the two armies, O Achyuta, until I can look at these men who wish to fight and see with whom I must battle in this war. Arjuna calls out to Achyuta, the unerring one, and asks him to place the chariot between the two armies so he can look at the men he must battle. Arjuna then asks Krishna to stop the chariot so he can see the men standing there, eager for battle.

verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Achyuta, keep my chariot between the two armies until I can inspect these men standing here, eager for battle, and see with whom I must fight in this great struggle.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Carrying on from the request to hold the chariot, Arjuna repeats his condition and asks one more thing before he looks.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Achyuta, keep my chariot between the two armies until I can inspect these men standing here, eager for battle, and see with whom I must fight in this great struggle. Arjuna repeats his wish to inspect the enemy, using the word yo'ttukaman, those desirous of fighting, which shows he is still thinking only as a warrior. He then asks to see the warriors who have gathered to fight for the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.

verses.sa: योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः । धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥
verses.tr: I want to see those who have gathered here, eager to fight and wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
verses.angle: Arjuna sees the motive of the enemy
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna asked Krishna to stop the chariot between the armies. Now he looks at the enemy and names the men on the other side. What does he see?

body.text: I want to see those who have gathered here, eager to fight and wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra. Arjuna does not call them his enemies. He calls them men who have come to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana. He names their motive before their faces. Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that Krishna placed the chariot right in front of Bhishma, Drona, and the kings.

next.title: Arjuna sees his own people across the field
